PhaseVectorResolution.status: NOT PINNED: registration section 4 does not define PhaseVectorResolution, its pixel numbers or scaledToDetector, and the oracle is written from the registration, not from the Swift. Amendment needed: state the definitions (inputs, outputs, formulas) in section 4.

chanceMatchFraction.definition: p = min(1, V rho^2 / R^2); cases have V >= 0, rho >= 0, R > 0
chanceMatchFraction.guards_UNREGISTERED: the registration does not say what R <= 0, V <= 0 or rho <= 0 return; the cases above only use V >= 0, rho >= 0, R > 0 (the formula gives 0 for V = 0 or rho = 0). The guard values of the source are NOT pinned: the registration needs an amendment (proposed: R <= 0 or a non-finite input returns 1, the safe 'cannot exclude chance').

cases.label: exact boundary: |v1 + v2| == radius, a pair under <=

containsFriedelPair.definition: UNREGISTERED in section 4, so this is the reading proposed here: some pair i < j with |v_i + v_j| <= radius (<=, as nearest). The pins record the minimum |v_i + v_j|. Flag edge: skip.

inPlaneSteps.definition: N = max(1, round(360/step)), round half away from zero; theta_k = k 2 pi / N; [0] for a step that is not finite, <= 0 or > 360. Steps 11 and 13 are added so that rounding and truncation differ (360/11 = 32.7, 360/13 = 27.7; mutant 5).

lowIndexZoneAxes.REGISTRATION_INCONSISTENCY: the registration says 62; the stated definition gives 49 (98 primitive vectors in the box, / 2 for sign). 62 = 124 / 2 is the count of the nonzero vectors deduplicated up to sign WITHOUT the gcd reduction (then [200] and [100] are two 'axes'): listed as alternative_unreduced. The apps-parity dump decides which the source computes.
lowIndexZoneAxes.definition: u, v, w in -2..2 (u outer, then v, then w), not all zero, / gcd, deduplicated up to sign, first representative kept

cases.label: exact boundary: d == rho, a hit under <= (mutant 6 turns it into a miss)

nearest.definition: closest reference within rho (<=); ties: the lowest index (flag tie: skip them in a test that does not register the rule); edge: a reference at |d - rho| <= 1e-12 (skip unless the case is the exact boundary)

score.definition: VARIANT A (pinned as 'score'): each experimental vector is assigned its nearest reference within rho; a reference's best distance is the least over its assigned vectors; the score is the mean over the unique references hit (null when none). The registration says 'the mean, over unique references hit, of their best distance': variant B (a reference is hit when any vector is within rho) is recorded as variant_any_pair; the cases where they differ are flagged variants_differ and a test must skip them unless the source's reading is confirmed.

euler.convention: R = M^T (crystal -> lab), extrinsic z-x-z: Rotation.from_matrix(R).as_euler('zxz'), wrapped to (-pi, pi]; crystal_to_lab = Rotation.from_euler('zxz', angles).as_matrix(); M is row-major (9 numbers)
euler.gimbal_rule_note: SciPy 1.18.1 locks when the middle angle is below 1e-7 (a scan of 400 random (phi1, phi2) each: 100% lock at 9.9e-8, 50% at exactly 1e-7, 0% at 1.01e-7), not at |sin Phi| <= 1e-8 as registration 4 says. The cases whose Phi_label is in rule_disagreement have rules_agree false: a Swift port that follows the registered 1e-8 gives phi2 != 0 there while SciPy gives 0 (the same rotation, different angles). Skip them or amend the registration to SciPy's rule; Phi = 1e-5 and 1e-6 are unlocked in both, so mutant 13 (threshold 1e-4) is still caught.

frame.definition: e1 = normalise(n x r), e2 = n x e1, r = x-hat if |n_x| < 0.9 else y-hat, n the Cartesian zone axis from the real lattice rows; q = (g.e1, g.e2); py4DSTEM: parse_orientation(zone_axis_lattice), p = (g.x', g.y')

frame_matrix_cases.definition: matrix = B R_z(a), R_z = [[c, s, 0], [-s, c, 0], [0, 0, 1]] (columns (c,-s,0), (s,c,0), (0,0,1)), row-major 9 numbers; the first 10 B are the columns (e1, e2, n) of the frame of the first 10 phase/axis pairs (an assumption about the basis layout: the product does not depend on it), then 10 seeded random rotations

oracles.V0: py4DSTEM Crystal.generate_diffraction_pattern at a huge accelerating voltage (lambda ~ 1e-26 A), sigma = w/sqrt(2), tol_excitation_error_mult = slab/sigma, tol_intensity 0: the 'py4dstem_*' fields of 'entries'
oracles.V1: NumPy flat excitation on py4DSTEM's own hkl, g and float32 |F|^2: the lambda -> 0 residual
oracles.V200: py4DSTEM at 200 kV, curved Ewald: the 'kv200' records
oracles.V2_reference: NumPy float64 from the registration's definitions (these pins' 'entries' and 'library')
